title: Learning to write music and the minor ninth chords
summary: Soloing and composing are tied together; a teacher showed him manuscript and a young woman at Howard showed him minor ninth chords, opening up composition.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did your composing develop as your trumpet playing developed? Let me re-phrase. Do you remember the first time, the first period that you felt I can compose also. I can offer something that can be a tune.

Yes. You know all of our original greats who created this, the realization is is that they are actually composing as they are soloing and it’s inextricably tied together, you know, soloing and composing. So you know, by example, Charlie Parker, all of his compositions are solos set down, scripted later, that became part of the underpinnings compositionally of this art form. Thelonious Monk etcetera. You know I mean Duke Ellington, you name it. And I think somewhere after I came back home from college I actually had started to write before I left college, and just you know my first songs you know I started to script them down. And there was a gentleman who is actually still alive, a wonderful musician that in my high school years he taught me how to set down things on manuscript. And from there my first couple of songs that came into my head I did that. And while at Howard University one day I was in the fine arts building of course, in one of the practice rooms, and I happened to pass by a room in which I was hearing these chords being played by a young lady and I knocked on the door and asked if I could come in and I said, “What is that you’re playing?” And she said, “Oh those are called ‘minor ninths.’” And I said, “Oh really, can you show me that?” And to this day that’s what I work off of. And she said to me, “Oh yes, my husband is John Hicks.” So they were teenagers I would imagine, they had to have been when they got married. And she went on to get her degree there at Howard. And of course I was to meet John shortly thereafter
in New York and of course the rest is history with that one with us as well. And it was those chords which, you know, open up compositional vistas for me, and arranging and orchestration and so on.
